Make Food Production and Equipment Performance Visible

Thematic Area: Food Manufacturing Intelligence & Production Efficiency

How might we connect production and equipment data to identify practical improvements in the output and consistency of prepared-food production?

Background

An Indonesian healthy-food retailer operates ready-to-eat, ready-to-heat and ready-to-cook product lines. The opportunity is to connect production and equipment data to support more efficient food manufacturing.

The objective is to establish a shared view of production steps, material movements, equipment use and output. This gives the operating team a practical basis for addressing capacity constraints, waiting, downtime and process variation.

Relevant startups offer manufacturing execution systems, equipment monitoring, industrial data integration and production analytics. The collaboration focuses on a selected production process and the decisions its operating data should support.

Significance of Problem

The key challenges are:

  • Unclear improvement priorities: A limited operating baseline makes it harder to direct investment towards the activities that contribute most to production performance.
  • Harder production planning: Limited visibility of actual output and equipment availability makes realistic production scheduling more difficult.
  • Unmeasured operating costs: Waiting, stoppages and repeated work consume production capacity and complicate operating-cost analysis.

Existing Efforts

  • Available capabilities: A manufacturing digitalisation provider offers production tracking, industrial IoT and internal material-movement automation. An equipment-monitoring platform consolidates machine, sensor and operating data to analyse performance and downtime.
  • First application: Select one production step and compare recorded input, saleable output, operating time and stoppage reasons with direct observation. Assign responsibility for reviewing the information and acting on it.
  • Collaboration focus: Connect relevant equipment and process records, set a practical data-capture method and define an improvement target. Track the effect of operating changes on output, downtime and cost.

Potential Market Size

  • Global production-software market: The manufacturing execution systems market was valued at US$17.6 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach US$41.6 billion by 2033, with 11.7% annual growth during 2026–2033. The market covers production software across manufacturing sectors.

Eligibility / Qualification

  • Technology readiness: Minimum technology readiness level 3 (TRL3).
  • NUS linkage: NUS student or graduate founder, or incubation through an NUS programme such as BLOCK71.
  • Local and overseas startups: Open to Indonesian and overseas startups.
  • Commitment: Complete the selection process and travel to Indonesia if selected.
